This is very close to Cafe Rio dressing.  So very good!
Wow, so yummy.  I didn't think the sour cream was overpowering at all.  Great flavors and saves a ton of time of having to do individual potatoes.  Definitely a family fav.
Charlotte, this was a tasty treat!  I have two little boys who eat me out of house and home, and this recipe received a resounding "YUM!"

I am a disaster in the kitchen but I decided to try this recipe today as it looked pretty easy.  Mine has turned out PERFECT.  My only difference was that I used a pork loin roast.  Thanks so much for sharing this as this definitely will be made again here and will be passed on.

I made this recipe as written but when I tried it after 5 hours of slow cooking, I felt it needed more flavour.  I added 1 cup of pureed tomatoes, 1 small clove of garlic, 1 tsp Italian herbs and then thickened it up with a few tbsps of tomato paste.  Then I cooked it for the final hour and added the cheese right before serving.  DH and I have been eating low carb for about 6 months now and it is great to have new recipes.  Thanks for sharing this.
OMG this is amazing!!!! I made with 2 cups of cilantro instead of parsley and no sugar. So so good!
We all loved this, was a nice change from regular chili. Thank you for a new great dish!
Very good Made my christmas cookie come out beautiful

My husband enjoyed this quite a bit.  He loves bbq and really likes pizza, so this was a can't miss.  I don't care for bbq so I didn't try it, but I did use the cheese suggestion (gouda and mozz) on a different pizza for me and it was to die for!  It made the pizza have a different but not too different taste.  I'd never tried gouda before and now I will use it all the time on pizzas for me.  So thank you from him for a great bbq chicken pizza and thank you from me for the idea to make my pepperoni pizza for me with gouda and mozzarella cheese.  We were both happy -- until we ran out of pizza.

Oh My Bergy, these are incredible. I was looking for something to go with our pot roast and my husband is very partial to biscuits. I choose this recipe because of it simplicity and (ok because it has great reviews) Now I know why. You can throw this together in minutes and still have a very fluffy, tender and buttery biscuit.  I am going to go with your suggestion and maybe add some herbs next time.  I have to say, these were especially tasty when soaking up the pot roast gravy.  Thank You so much for sharing!
I make this every Christmas and Thanksgiving and there's never any left over! Very indulgent!

I made this for DH and the guests tonight. 4 people had it and the comments went from "OMG! it's sweet, ewwwww" to "I think this is one of the best meatloaves I've ever had". The other two were quite favorable so it gets a 4 star rating. The apples were fine, the controversy came from the sugar. Even with the onion, Worcestershire and mustard the sugar came through. I guess weather thats a good or a not so good thing depends on personal taste. I put it in the small crock pot and it got almost the full 9 hrs. It was moist and had a lovely aroma and it sliced well. I served it with mashed potato's, corn and peas mixed and hot biscuits with honey.
These were awesome!  I made them for a dinner recently and my guests both said they were the best they had ever eaten.  I don't even like crab cakes - but these were yummy.

This is great and a keeper! I will probably never buy applesauce at the store again. I used 4 Gala apples that we had sitting (because our primary apple-eater is currently out of town). After reading other reviews, I decreased the sugar by a Tablespoon (so I just used 3 Tablespoons), and I used 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon and 1/4 teaspoon apple pie spice for the spices. It also took my apples about 40 minutes to soften before I mashed them with a potato masher. This was my first time making homemade applesauce, and it was so easy. Thanks for sharing your father's recipe!

REALLY REALLY DELICIOUS.  I love the pineapple and lemon zest!
Refreshing in the heat.

AND there's NO stinky garlic - YAY!

I was not a coleslaw fan. . . . until now.  This was so easy to make using the food processor. I used a lite whipped dressing and it was perfect.  This will be great for those summer BBQ's with friends.  Thanks dale.

3 stars because we just "liked it."  I think 6-8 hours is too long for cubed steaks that already have been browned.  The "steaks" just fall apart.  I did love the fact that it was easy and required a handful of ingredients though.  Maybe I'll try it again without cooking so long.

I made this when I was trying to use up some of my tomatoes, and it was really good.  I added some frozen shrimp (because I was trying to use that up too) and didn't do the onion ring thing at the end.  I didn't think it needed it.  Even the kids liked it, (and they normally don't touch tomatoes!)  I served it with rice, naan bread, and a lentil curry.  Will definitely make it again!

I tried it and it's YUM!!!  I couldn't believe it.  If you've got 2 mins. then you've got a great - on the go - sandwich to eat.  You can even make it at work which is just great for me.  I have english muffins here.  Put one egg and a slice of cheese in a baggie, bring it here and fix it up.  Wonderful!

Thanks for sharing!

Made this recipe the other night and we really liked the concept and felt it had good potential but the chicken was so dry. (The inside drippings were really tasty though) Any suggestions for what we could do?

I got a late start on this and didn't feel comfortable having it simmer during the night. I pulled out my pressure cooker, followed the recipe unaltered, then threw everything in set it for high pressure, gave it 55 minutes, let it release pressure naturally, and it was amazing! I love this recipe! It's easy and takes me back to supper at nana's on Sunday's. I served it German style over mashed potatoes and was in heaven!

This was quite good. I did as other reviewers suggested in that I added 1 Tablespoon of cornstarch and 1 Tablespoon of water (separately) into the sauce, stirring the sauce very well, towards the end of the cooking, to thicken. I served it on rice with some chopped green onions (the green parts) sprinkled on top.
This was part of a dinner I was throwing for my son (19, woohoo!) and his friends. This dish was the favorite. Thank you LinMarie.
IT SEEMS LIKE TO MUCH TROUBLE, BUT I BET IT'S DELICIOUS !

Delicious! I followed the other reviewers' suggestions, and sauteed the onion, along with some chopped celery, before adding to the other ingredients. I also added some shredded carrots. Finally, I subbed in barbecue sauce for half the tomato sauce, and it gave it a nice smoky flavor. This was really delicious, and I didn't have a problem with it being crumbly. I will definitely make this again!

A great, easy comfort recipe! I was looking for a variation on macaroni and cheese for a family meal.  I used 2 cans of 98% fat free cream of chicken, changed the cheese to what I had (4 oz 50% cheddar and 4 oz light mexican blend. My husband raved about the taste.  Next time I might try to sneak in broccoli or tomatoes for a one dish meal.  A definite keeper.  Thanks for sharing!

Wow.  This recipe is very easy, but not fast.  It took me a while to peel and slice the 14 peaches.  However, it was well worth it.  The combination of ingredients was spot on for me, not too sweet.  The peach flavor really comes through, of course, it's the peak of peach season so that really helps.  I will be making this again.  It took an additional 20 minutes to bake mine but maybe my peaches were too juicy.  I did add 1 tablespoon corn starch into the fruit as there was so much juice I was worried it would come out too soggy.  I also sprinkled the top with turbinado sugar for the last 10 minutes just to give it that sparkly look.

Great recipe to make first of the week. But you would think the leftovers would last till the weekend... not the case! I threw in a large 5.7 lb chuck roast in along with the season packs. At first I was a bit worried about that size of a roast being dry. No way, it was falling apart just from me trying to handle it. I put 1 cup of water along with some baby carrots and quartered potatoes. Completely juicy and flavorful!! Thank you for sharing. Oh and I did sear the sides of the roast prior to cooking in the pot. This may or may not have helped but it turned out so great I wouldn't think of doing it any other way.

Thanks Again!!
yep another Kitten winner, Kit this is amazing,we had it over mashed potatoes, so so so so good, thank you.

This recipe makes a perfect Honey Mustard Dressing.  I followed the recipe exactly and found it a little thin, so I put it in the blender and drizzled some Canola oil in while running and it thickened up nicely.  I also found the oil rounded out the flavors and gave the dressing a nice mouth feel.

I made these last night with fried chicken and corn on the cob and it was REALLY good!
I will for sure be making thses again, my family gobbled them up.
and Inez's ultimate strawberry shortcake for dessert! it was a fantastic meal

I love risotto in general and I love this variation of it, too.  I did not use the mushrooms or hot sauce and it was still delicious.  It was creamy and full of flavor.  I wasn't sure what to do with the ground beef as the recipe never mentioned it after cooking it.  So, I added about 1/2 pound back in at the same time I added the butter, sour cream, and parmesan.  To me 1 pound would have been WAY too much.  1/2 pound was perfect.  Thanks for the recipe.

I have made this recipe time and time again and it always turns out delightful.  My dad is diabetic so I use Splenda instead of sugar and it is one of his absolute favorites.  My husband recently started watching his sugar intake so I made this to take to his family's house on Christmas.  It was a hit there also, even with the Splenda.  Thanks sugar pea for this great recipe!

Very good!  My family does not like spicy food and with the Red Pepper flakes it gets spicy!  So next time I will make it without but otherwise I followed it to the Tee and it was very good and easy to make.  We will make this a family favorite!
We really enjoyed this very filling take on a Greek salad - it was a perfect side to grilled pork tenderloin on a very hot summer evening. Thanks for sharing!

Pork-O-Lucious ! I've had this recipe in my box for a few months. I was waiting for the weather to get cool enough so that I could have my oven on for several hours.The day finally came! I had some concerns. When I went to find a Picinc Shoulder Roast, all that I could find were smoked-(more like a ham that you would bake). I finally settled on a Pork Shoulder Blade. The largest I could find weighed 6 and a half pounds. Out came the calculator, and I got the roasting time down to the minute.It was SO worth the math stress :)!
Served this with some collards, and beans and rice.Sublime. Thankyou so much.

Fantastic recipe.  My family gobbled them up. The second time around I added chopped apple, cinnamon and dried currants.  We now make enough oatmeal to have leftovers just for these muffins.  Don't be afraid to use whole wheat flour.
Good foundation but it was missing something. I am not sure what...It was not good.
Leanne thanks for sharing this recipe. Was a wonderful! I added fetticini noodles and topped it off with bread crumbs and topped it off with cheese. Can't wait to try it in a pot pie.
Very good!  I did only use one tomato and about half a cucumber because my family does not like veggies so I can only sneak in a few.  Thanks!!
I didn't use whole wheat couscous as others did and perhaps should have as I was not fond of this.  I found the basil overpowering.

This recipe is absolutely delicious! I put this on a chocolate cake and it's the perfect pairing. However, it was a little heavy. To help this I whipped the frosting once finished on high for about 2-3 minute is my stand mixer. This not only made more frosting so that I could easily frost a two-layered cake, but aerated the frosting making it lighter and much fluffier.
I made this pizza this afternoon and I loved it so much!  I used bacon bits on top and it was good but I think real bacon crumbles would be better. So so good.

Big hit in our family!  After reading the reviews, I opted to add an 8-oz. can of tomato sauce to make sure there was enough sauce - we love sauce.  When all the components were ready, I mixed it all together, more like a goulash than chili.  We loved it that way, though I'm sure it's no longer authentic koshari.   It's great comfort food, and it reheats in the microwave like a dream, which is good, because this recipe makes a ton.  Thank you for sharing this recipe, Sackville.

Thank you for this recipe.  It has a great tang to it and I have used it as a dip for veggies, crackers and chips.   I also used it as a spread on sandwiches.  Everyone likes it whoever I serve it to.  I will keep this in the frig often.  I made it exactly as written.  I used the Grey Poupon dijon mustard and canola mayonnaise for a little less fat.
This is the most beautiful dish I have had for a long time.  We added grilled Haloumi cheese and Macadamia Nuts with it.  Will be adding it to the "Make regularly list"

What a great recipe,great taste and so easy.My husband and I have only been married a short time he is Greek and I am Aussie and he thinks I am getting as good as his mother. Thanks Heaps.he doesn't need to know where I get all these great recipes from.Thanks Again

Oh my goodness.  You know that feeling you get in the joint of your jaw when something is so tart it threatens to eat the enamel off your teeth, but your tongue tells your jaw and teeth to shut up because it's enjoying the food too much and they are killing it's buzz?  You know that feeling?  You must have eaten these strawberries before then, because that is exactly the feeling we had while eating them!  My roommate and I scarfed a half recipe, completely unwilling to share with either children or menfolk.  Thank you Potsie, Oh, thank you for posting this!  Made for ZWT4.

We love your spaghetti! This is my husband's favorite dinner. I use half ground beef and half sausage, and I add a chopped green pepper with the onion. Otherwise, I make it exactly as written. We use one quart the day I make it and freeze the remaining three for easy weeknight meals. Thank you for this fabulous recipe.

I made this for Mother's Day this year. Everyone was skeptical when I told them the name of our dessert, but it got rave reviews from even the pickiest eater. The ingredients in the fresh fruit salsa blend into a scrumptious burst of favors, and grilling the angel cake warms it just enough to bring out the flavor.

I am very aware of too much sugar in my diet so I always cut the sugar in half when I can.  This ended up being perfect for me with half the sugar.  I am bringing it along for tomorrow's picnic.  Thank you soooo much for this super salad with two of my favorite things spinach and strawberries!
This was a good warm dip with a flavor kick.  I served it in a small crockpot during my holiday open house.  I omitted the pecans and offered tortilla chips for dipping.
Pretty good, we used spaghetti sauce, and added some veggies, it also took about 15 mins.   Thanks for posting!

My family has been using this recipe since I was a child (with the exception of we use 1 stick of butter rather than margarine), and we love it.  I made it last night for a BBQ, and got SOOOOOO many compliments and requests for the recipe.

My advice is to start checking it around 40-45 minutes, as the pecans on top can burn, and it is often done by 45 minutes.  We also recommend using chopped pecans rather than pecan halves, as the larger nuts tend to burn more quickly.  When I took it out of the oven last night at 45 minutes, I ended up having to pick off some burned nuts, but otherwise it was perfect!

So good! Sounded yummy, and tasted even better than expected, even with low fat mayo and nonfat sour cream. I added double the dill (fresh), used chopped cornichons (relish would have made it too sweet), and instead of half to half I used 3/4 of the sour cream to 1/4 of the mayo, since I am not a big mayo person. I made half of this recipe and could almost finish it in one non-piggy snacking/dipping session. It went well with Baked Ruffles. Perfect balance of flavors!

I made this for our family reunion, and it was a big hit! I was concerned about using the oil, but not baking it, but it turned out fine, not at all greasy like I thought it might be. My package sizes were a little off, but as close as I could get.  The Ritz Bits miniatures were actually sandwiches with cheese inside, which made it even more yummy.  Thanks so much for posting a recipe so much tastier than the Chex mix!

I am so thrilled to have found this recipe.  My mom used to make "DILLY BEANS" when I was a child.  They are wonderful and you need to hide them, or your kids will eat them all up.
Thanx for posting.

Only the 2 of us for Thanksgiving so I wanted the taste of sweet potatoes and the texture of mashed potatoes.  This was perfect.  The spices are just right on this.  Not too sweet, not too savory.  The flavor of the potatoes really come through and the nuts are a good contrast.  The top cracked a little and I wonder if more nuts or a finer chop, perhaps with some butter on top might prevent that.  Will definitely make again.

It is fabulous! I always add a little extra salt at the end and it just sets the flavor off perfectly!I also use nonfat cream yogurt to make it a little healthier and is still tastes fab.  My family now always requests this to be among the dishes when I am cooking an indian dinner!
Great authentic recipe. Yes, to other comments, it is salty. Poke is a very salty dish, this is dead on point for flavor and salt. Ma'halo bruddah!

You & another RZ chef convinced me again that the lowly meatloaf does not have to be boring. I made only 1 sml chg out of necessity & used dried cilantro instead of fresh. This is mildly southwestern if you apply an adventurous flavor std, but the lovely surprise here was how much I enjoyed the sweetness of the brown sugar combined w/the savory flavors of garlic, hot sauce, cilantro & worcestershire. This worked very well for us & will be repeated. Thx for sharing the recipe w/us.
Just like my Mom's ---simple--sweet and tart. Delicious. Thanks for posting, Mimi.
These are truely amazing. I made them for my daughter's birthday party and every girl ate them up!!! I will definitely be making these again.
Good base recipe.  My kids loved the flavor - light and sweet!  Easy to add fruit before baking or as a topping.

I followed the instructions as written, although I did add 1 cup of water around the edge at the end. Cooked on low for 4 1/2 hours and it came out perfect. It's a very good base, but a little bland as is. Tweaking it just a little, with sausage and/or some of your favorite herbs, will make this a keeper for life.
Sorry, didn't much like the flavor & texture combo

Great tahini balls! I used very soft dates and a very liquid tahini, but they are sticking together very well and taste very yummy. Thanks for sharing!
Made for Let's Go To Saudi Arabia / N*A*M*E Forum

Lovely, tasty cake; who would have thought that humble buttermilk could make a pound cake taste this good?? I actually ended up making 3/4 of the recipe - I know from past (bitter) experience that my bundt pan is a bit too small for 4-egg-3-cups-of-flour cake, so I scaled this down a bit. Worked beautifully! I used fat-free buttermilk and 2 ts of vanilla sugar instead of the extracts. Also reduced the oven temperature to 150 C as my pan is dark and coated (and thus tends to produce a hard crust on cakes if I use the specified temp.), and baked for about 1 hour and 10 minutes. Yum! Thanks for a great recipe!

Excellent version of this classic recipe.  It had the perfect mix of sweet/sour tang, and just the right amount of dressing for the beans.  I'm placing this one in my favorite salads cookbook, and you can be sure it will be made often, because it's so easy to make before chilling it overnight.

We made these as Babies In Blankets for my daughters birthday party. They would be perfect for a baby shower or something, too. I used regular hot dogs cut in half and packaged crescent dough. I didn't use any sauce, but did sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese inside. We had side bowls of mustards and ketchup for dipping. I used a toothpick and a knife to make little eyes and mouths; happy, sad sleeping, etc. And they really did turn out adorable- and DELICIOUS! They were gone early.

These were really good.  I hate "smushy" mashed sweet potatoes with all the stuff that people put with them for Thanksgiving.  It hides the true flavor of the sweet potatoes.  I omitted the balsamic vinegar, and sliced mine into big "rounds" about 1/2 to 1' thick.  They were lovely to look at, too, with the edges starting to brown.  I think this recipe may have converted my inlaws away from the "brown sugar and marshmallows" sweet potatoes!

This is a keeper. I would have post pictures but entire casserole was eaten so quickly there was no time for pictures. I did not have a couple of things like sour cream, so that was omitted and for cream I used 2% milk, all cheese used was shredded cheddar and oh yeah...no pork so no bacon juice. I'm a cajun girl so Tony Cachere seasoning is a must as season salt...Everything was DELICIOUS. Kittencal I Love Your ideas and have tried a number of your recipes. All very SATISFYING... keep posting.
I feel terrible giving only 3 stars but this was just not a hit with me and DH. Tasty enough, and a nice different sweet taste but I probably won't be making it again. I'd prefer more of a BBQ taste

I love the idea of flavors here, they really work well! I used the recipe as is except I used honey mustard dressing instead of the fisrt 2 and then coated the legs in breadcrumbs. Baked for 35 min and perfection!

This turkey is moist, flavorful, and worth all of the work! I made this for thanksgiving and loved it- my dh didnt like it, but that is  because he is a traditionalist who thinks that turkey should be plain.  Thanks so much for sharing!

Oh my gosh the last time I ate this, I was a kid! I really wanted to make this recipe with my child and that is exactly what I did, and we had lot's of fun making the meatballs! This is really great and I served it along with mashed potatoes and a salad. Thanks so much Chipotlechick..... love your name ChipotleChick
This was sort of ordinary but I am sure little kids would gobble it up! Something was definitely missing. Sorry, we didn't care for it very much :(

I remember having these cookies as a kid and wanted to find a good recipe to make them for my children.  This is exactly how I remember them tasting.  So delicious and so so easy.  Thanks for posting!
My kids loved these and ate half the pan, then I ate the other half. Very addicting. I used butter & Multi Grain Cheerios. We will make these often!

*Reviewed during ZWT5 Family Picks for Australia with Chow Hounds Team* My family enjoyed this burger as it was a little different to our norm. The Vegemite took place of salt in the recipe and added extra savoury flavour. Miracle Whip seems to be a recent addition to our supermarket shelves and my non-mayo husband actually liked it. Through all the eating noises...the only grumble that I heard was that little tummies were getting way to full.....but they kept on eating and none was left! Thanks for a yummy family-friend;y meal that was really easy to put together. We served with home-made potato wedges on the side. Photo also being posted

I had about 4# of Roma Tomatoes from my garden that I wanted to use so I modified this recipe to use fresh ingredients and it was very good.  I didn't use any canned tomatoes, sauce or paste, just 4# of fresh, quartered, Romas which I roasted at 450F for about 40 minutes (with olive oil, onion, garlic, salt, pepper, and a 1/2 chopped green pepper just because I had it).  I assumed the herbs (oregano, thyme, rosemary, etc.) were all dried measurements so I tripled the measurement (1T instead of 1t) to use my fresh garden herbs.  The color was light but flavor was full.  We will try it over pasta tomorrow.  Seems like it would be a good base for a vodka sauce.
Very tasty.  However I found it required an extra 10mins in the oven.  Yum!

I substituted pork for beef and the results were brilliant. No need to tweak or modify this one. Just started cooking for the first time in thirty years. This was my 5th meal and the whole family were amazed at the flavours.

Wonderful leek dish, the only things I did different were, cutting up the leeks and I added grated nutmeg to the sauce. Next time I will broably leave out the breadcrumbs, add the cheese to the sauce and then bake for 10-15 minutes

The squash did not cook in the time suggested and it was a real pain to scoop out the squash without demolishing the shell.  I ended up scooping all the squash out, mixing with ingredients and cooking in a buttered baking dish.  The flavor was good so I will make this again, but will peel and cube the squash before baking it at 400 for 45 minutes.

These were delicious my family and some neighborhood kids loved them. I made them almost exactly as written except I used a pork tenderloin that I had cooked in the crockpot.  Filled and fried them and everyone was happy. Thank you for this great recipe.

This is so easy & flavorful even my meat-loving DH enjoyed it. I whipped this up quickly on a crazy weeknight, serving with warmed whole-wheat tortillas, shredded lettuce, cheddar cheese, low-fat sour cream & hot sauce. I think it would also be great to stir in any leftover rice or chopped tomatoes into the bean mixture. I'll definitely make this easy, delish, low-fat meal again!
Yum! Delicious cinnamon gluten free muffins. Good with cream cheese frosting or plain! :)

WOW! This was fabulous and didn't take long to disappear! I made this for ZWT4 team Kumquat's Kookin' Kaboodles. Thanks for sharing- ~Sue

Definitely will cook this again, it was really good. Made a few tweeks..added cbpped green pepper, fresh chopped garlic and basil, and crushed red pepper. Also took off the foil and let it cook for another 10minutes to brown the top.

What a great recipe for the grill.  Living in Florida I am always looking for grilling recicpes and this is a keeper.  I only made enough for one and it worked out well.  Thanks Kittencal for another wonderful recipe!!!!

I made this for my husband and he really enjoyed them alot!  I cut the recipe in half, using less than half the amount of breadcrumbs with no problems.  I used Italian bread crumbs for extra flavour.  I baked them in my fan oven so they browned nicely, but also didn't need to bake for the required time, taking instead only about 20 minutes.  Very easily put together using things I always have in my pantry, this is a recipe I am sure I will repeat.  Thanks so much!

When I presented this I was told it is called a "Rusty" Screwdriver". Oh well, what's in a name. A sea breeze certainly comes to mind when drinking this. Used freshly squeezed orange juice and it was very good to sit down with this drink after a day of work. Thanks for posting. made for My-Three-Chefs, June '08.

YUM! The Marinade for the chicken was awesome! I did add some Cavender's Greek seasoning to it, and sprinkled some on the chicken before grilling on my George Forman grill.  I used a little extra yogurt than called for, also my yogurt was thickened by straining it overnight first. I added a little salt too. I served it with some to-die-for Lebonese pita breads that I bought,  and served it more of a gyro style with lettuce and thinly sliced red onion as the toppings.  Absolutely Wonderful!

My daughter and I had these for a snack tonight.  We also used portobella mushrooms, the soy sauce and garlic gives this a very nice flavor.  Just the right amount of both as not to be overpowered by one flavor.  If we ever get a photo taken, it well be due to the fact that we made a double batch so we can eat as we photo the other!!  Thank you, Mark adding this one to our favorites.

This is definitely a 5 star dish.  I did not have thighs and legs so I used 4 boneless/skinless breasts.  I also used a jalapeno pepper in place of one of the green peppers.   I really like this sauce.  Made for ZWT5, Dining Daredevils.

So easy and so good -- a perfect endiing to a spicy meal. I didn't have any of the liquor so I used some extract instead -- delicious! This is great alone or would be a delicious topping for pound cake. Thanks Evelyn for posting this keeper desert recipe. We will be making this often this summer.

I made it as both muffins as well as cake!! Every1 loved it at home..! Its been three days and yet I am begged to make it again!! Simply splendid recipe! So soft..SOooo yumm! haha! And this was my first try in baking anything for the first time in my life! :D So much more happier! Love you for sharing this recipe..! I tweaked it a bit tho'.. instead of buttermilk.. I added milk.. But still it tasted marvellous!! Thank you!! :D
Yummy! The entire family loved this recipe. It's a keeper.
The flavor was good but I may have overcooked it a bit as I found the rice a bit dry but then that may just be the way basmati rice is. Thanks for the recipe I'll try it again.

These were fantastic!  When I first chose this recipes, I didn't notice how much mustard was in this and I was a little skeptical about whether I would like it or not (I'm not a yellow mustard fan) as two tablespoons seems like a lot, but it really isn't.  I also was not able to find a suitable buffalo wing sauce due to my allergies so I used Frank's Red Hot sauce instead.  DH couldn't stop raving about these.  The flavors blend wonderfully.  I think this recipe would also work well in the crock pot.  Will definitely make these again!  Thanks for posting this Lainey.  Made for 1~2~3 Hits.

Serving sauce over rice  & chops.

This was pretty good chicken.  It didn't have the flavor pop that I would have liked, but I can't ever seem to find one that just "pops".  It was beautiful!  I put it on my grill along with some slices of vadalia onions and brushed them right along with the chicken.  The onions turned out pretty good too.

Served with baked potatoes, sour cream, peas dabbed with butter.  Thanks for the nice dinner!

I loved the combination of pasta and cabbage mix.  I didn't have tahini so I just threw in some sesame seeds with the onions and green pepper.  I used boneless, skinless chicken thighs cut into pieces and chopped sweet onion.  It wasn't as flavorful as I would have thought but my curry was probably old and I hesitated to use more because my family does not like spicy food.  They did like this however and adding a bit of soy sauce once it was served on the plate helped a lot.  I will definitely make this again and even try a teryaki version.

I made these potatoes to accompany a roast chicken. I par boiled my potatoes for a few minutes to make them tender and yet crisp them up when baked. Only change I made was using fresh parmesan. My family loved them and DS has already requested these again. Great recipe Jelisa!

This was very good...I find that the longer you cook turnips the sweeter they become...cooking them al dente is probably why they were a bit nippy...my family loved them and they don't care much for veggies...Great recipe!

I made this using 2 tablespoons olive oil because of the healthier fat then butter. I used maple syrup in place of the maple extract and corn syrup, plain walnuts. Delish. I did grill it 5 minutes per side. Made for ZWT6 Thanks.

This is wonderful!  I made it for my husband's birthday and it was a treat!  I used chicken broth instead of water with the saffron.  Also added chopped onions with the garlic and peas into the pasta the last minute of cooking.  YUM-O!

This was my first time ever making brussel sprouts. My boyfriend said he loves them so I thought I'd give these a try, and he said these were great. I didn't understand the point of cutting an x into the stem and then cutting them in half.

It looks as though I'm number #35 to rate your Salmon Patties recipe, unless another review is posted before mine.  My husband loved these patties, too. I'll be making them again, and soon. Meanwhile I added some more cans of salmon and another box of Ritz crackers to my grocery list, so I won't run out of supplies. I liked the fact that these are easy to make and can be ready in a short amount of time.  I followed you recipe exactly.  Thanks Mary!  Joje
I made this one day and my children fell in love with it. I added potatoes to it as well it's a great and easy meal. The potatoes makes it a much hearty meal.
I have to say that this was a great recipe! My whole family loved it. I even shared "a little" with the neighbors, and they gave me a big thumbs up! Thanks Jill4man for a wonderful recipe.

It seems that most are happy with your recipe :) I have a go to recipe for cream pies as well. I had never tried cooking the coconut with the milk. I always stir it in before I pour the filling in the crust. I only use 2cups of scalded milk, 2/3 cup sugar and 1/3 cup of flour. Three egg yolks slightly beaten, 1 Tablespoon vanilla and 1 T butter. This recipe makes great banana pudding as well. I will try yours next time. :)
I made these cupcakes for a wedding shower.... can you say wow?  They were a hit! Light and refreshing on a summer afternoon. Everyone wanted the recipe.  I highly recommend!

I actually just used the dressing from this recipe to toss with a regular old romaine leaf salad. And as it turns out I was out of Red Wine Vinegar and Olive Oil, so I used Raspberry Balsamic Vinegar and Grape Seed Oil mixed with the pepper and Parmesan Cheese. It turned out great!!
Made these for my daughter's baby shower and boy did they go over well. Going to make them again this weekend for family game night.

I thought this was a fantastic drink.  I only used about a tablespoon of the orange zest, but other than that, made as directed.  My daughter really liked this and it was perfect on a hot, humid night.  Thanks Lynda

Made as directed for OAMC's Freezer Tag Game.  
Froze in one quart containers.
After thawing one container in the fridge overnight, heated it up and served with penne pasta and garlic bread.  So yum!
Great recipe...thanks for sharing.
I made a few alterations but liked this as a base recipe.

I rarely leave reviews, even for things I love. But for this recipe, I MUST stop and join the chorus singing praises.  This chicken is amazing, and I am so excited to serve it to guests tonight! I made it ahead of time so it could sit (someone said it tastes even better the next day) and excluded the peppers and cilantro for my picky eaters. Thank you so much for sharing such an outstanding recipe!!

I am fairly new to crockpot cooking (even though I'm 52 years old) but when I saw this recipe a light went off "NOT ENOUGH LIQUID" the light kept telling me.  After barely 4 hours in the crockpot on low, I returned home to a foul smell.  I went to the crockpot and pulled off the lid - I had a big burned on gooey mess (no, I did not add the cheese or rice).  Like other reviwers, I feel that the time specified is way too long and/or the liquid amount is NOT enough.  Imagine had I not been home until the meal was suppsoed to be ready......I can't imagine what a mess I would have found.  I think someone needs to go back and double-check the amounts specified in this recipe.

My five year old help to make the batter while I did the veggies which turned out well. Good recipe that the kids can help with...and nothing like tempura to have kids eating vegetables they normally don't like to eat!

I had a little difficulty with my meringue, so I'm giving this only 4 stars.  The lemon filling was excellent though.  The recipe itself with a little time consuming, but none of it difficult. Perhaps the second time around will be perfect.  I will make this again.

Ohhhhh man! These pancakes were awesome.  My mom claimed they were the best she ever had! They were very moist.  I only used about 1 tbsp. of honey because that is all I had, however, I threw in a little bit of sugar so it was still sweet.  I don't think it made any difference! I actually made an apple topping to go along with it and it really went well with the pancakes.  I added raisins also to the pancakes.  I will make these again and again!
I've made these twice since Thursday. So fast and easy and my kids just love them. We like them quite "done" so I leave them in the oven for the maximum baking time.

This was seriously good!  Made exactly to recipe.  I used Devil's Food Cake Mix.  Think I will possibly use some cherry juice as noted by another reviewer.  Thnx for posting, Tonkcats.  Made for Comfort Cafe Summer 2009.

I have made this twice now, once on low for 8 hours, once on high for 4 hours, and both times it came out AMAZING.  I used TJ's chicken mango sausage, and substituted Craisins for the raisins. I didn't have allspice, so I used a little extra cinnamon, a little ginger, and a little ground cloves.  (And when I say "a little", I mean a couple of shakes.)

Finally, and most importantly, THE TYPE OF RICE YOU USE MAKES A HUGE DIFFERENCE! I have seen a few comments that this dish comes out mushy, but I found the perfect rice that adds a fabulous texture: Trader Joe's "Brown Rice Medley". Yes, it takes forever to cook, but it's so worth it!

Thanks for posting this so I won't lose it either. ;-)

This was my first time to ever make or taste Irish soda bread. I made it for our St. Patrick's Day family get-together. It was wonderful. Very light in texture and the caraway seed adds so much to the flavor. I can't imagine anyone leaving this ingredient out. I am bread-making challenged and I thought this recipe was very easy to make. Thanks 1Steve.

My family and I have been eating spinach Fandango for the past 40 years. If you put it on a bed of rice it tastes much better than just eating it like it comes out of the pan. I use cream of mushroom soup instead of the celery never heard of using cream of celery cream of mushroom just tastes awesome. I use Uncle Ben's boil in a bag rice. That is very simple to use Cooks easily and taste great doesn't stick.
I love this candy! I make it all the time, although, sometimes I use spearmint oil too.
heeey isnt this a paula deen recipe with the noodle type changed? shes so good. Im going thru cooking almost everything in her book since my mom in law gave them to me!

I made this for my boyfriend and I for Valentines day... It turned out really tasty..It was almost like a thick piece of fudge or a brownie... I used raspberry jam and the liquor for the sauce and served it with whipped cream... very yummy! though I had to cook it almost 20 minutes extra.

This was our Christmas Eve dinner.  Brilliant!  The flavor is fantastic, complex and each component comes through perfectly.  I had to use dried tarragon (1 tsp.) but it tasted wonderful in there.  The broth is heavenly!  We also added a little rice to each bowl, and served with crusty bread to soak up the broth.  Wonderful, memorable meal!  (Sorry the photo is so lousy - time for a better camera!)

Your salsa is soooooo good!  I used the "mild" rotel tomatoes and green chilies and it was just the right amount of "bite" for us - also added a couple of chopped plum tomatoes. Served this when family visited for Easter and it was a huge hit with everyone.  I like that this recipe makes an ample amount for serving company. Thanx for a great recipe, Melanie!

OMG, I can't believe I've found this recipe after all these years!  As a kid growing up there was a corner store in our neighborhood that was run by an elderly couple who raised chickens and made these pickled eggs and sold them in their store.  Dad and I loved them and he would buy them for us when we would stop in now and then.  They gave my mom the recipe and she & I would make them as well, but the recipe was lost over the years, and I just couldn't recall all the ingredients.  I raise chickens now and have wished many times that I had this recipe.  Thank you so much for sharing.

My son likes to dip soda crackers in storebought Ranch dressing for a snack, so he decided to try this. Very easy, he said, and tasty. The flavor definitely improves the longer it sits, so try to make it a day ahead of when you'll need to use it.

My husband loves cauliflower so I am always looking for new ways to cook it. He enjoyed this recipe but he said that there was too much onion and he loves onions. Next time I make it I will only use half an onion. Thanks Sydney Mike...
So good! Eating it now :) now I know exactly what I'll bring to a summer lunch or picnic. You gotta be crazy not to like this! Thanks for sharing.

Just wanted to let you know that I just got a new KitchenAid stand mixer and debated on what to make first.   I decided on this recipe for cinnamon buns.    They were wonderful, and I received compiments from everyone that shared one.    I was a bit intimidated by the 3 1/2 hour prep time, but as I tell my children often... "anything in life worth having takes effort".    Thanks for this recipe.

This dish was unfortunately just ok for us; a good basic side, but no wow factor. I reduced the quantity by 1/3. The serving size is very generous and can easily be reduced. Made for Everyday is a Holiday Tag.

I was looking for a recipe to use up some things in the fridge and pantry before going on vacation. I used this recipe as my base. I only had 2 potatoes left, totalling 1/4 lb. For the remaining 3/4 lb.+ I subbed zucchini. I first steamed the zucchini and onions and pureed them in the blender (they are vegetables of which my children are not fond). At the same time I covered the beans and potatoes with water and cooked. Afterward I combined them along with a cup of milk and 2T of butter. Added salt and pepper (no thyme) and everyone enjoyed it. Thank you lets.eat for helping to accomplish my goal with your simple recipe.

I suggest the salt and pepper, but very delicious and super easy! P.s. I put it over noodles, my preference! I also didn't have 6-8 hrs to "prepare" this meal so I cooked it on high for 4-5hrs and the chicken was all the way done! Yummy! :)

This is the fastest, quickest, yummiest way to make banana bread!  I did do a couple of things differently...I made it in a 9"x13" pan and baked it for 33 minutes (until a pick came out clean).  I just put the bananas in the bowl (I used 5 bananas--had some peeled ones in baggies in the freezer...put them in there whenever they are too far gone to eat) with the rest of the ingredients and mashed them there) and I added about 1/2 cup mini milk chocolate chips!  I think this is going to be my new way to make banana cake!  Moist and not crumbly! Thanks for a great recipe!

this is a wonderful recipe.  my darling husband who will only eat 4 french fries (!) absolutely adored this and was even caught nibbling before i could finish laying the table.  will never make french fries again!!!

I needed a vanilla sauce for bread pudding and was out of cornstarch so i tried this recipe.  YUM!  I cooked it down until it was the consistency of thick syrup.  It was very quick and easy to make and i will be making again.

Delicious pot roast. The gravy is very flavorful; I was eating it with a spoon! I did not have molasses so I substituted honey. Really good served with mashed potatoes, peas, carrots, Cole slaw, and fresh Italian bread slices. For the Cole slaw, I used a portion of bagged Cole slaw, available in the supermarket, and set aside the rest of it to make fried cabbage or cabbage soup. I set aside some cooked meat for sandwiches, and am making a shepherds pie with leftover mashed potatoes on top today.

Made these for the first time tonight for a Christmas party. Really creative, and everyone seemed to like them. Great in the midst of dessert-heavy holiday parties. Will experiment in the future to make it a little less bland, but great recipe.

Avery nice recipe if you don't want too sweet!  And with the addition of the cream cheese mixture minus the chocolate chips, it steps right up to the plate!  I just realized when I was reading the review from Chef #1321165 that I had forgotten the chips!  But I don't think we will miss them, Nan.  Thnx for posting.  Made for Comfort Cafe Summer 2009.
I've made this on several occasions and love it myself but I also have tons of people asking for the recipe too.  Great for a brunch or breakfast.

Delicioso!! My first stew ever and it was so good! I added kidney beans like Prose did and it gave it a great texture to it. Very easy and fun to make on a rainy/cloudy/snowy day. I gave it 4 stars because I felt it needed something else...but that's just me. Enjoy!!

P.S thanks Prose.

This is super easy for a quick weekday meal. I added the mushrooms on top since only my husband likes them. I also added garlic powder to the seasonings. There was not enough sauce to adequitely cover the noodles, so I would double the amount of sour cream next time. The wine added an upscale touch to this recipe. Thanks for sharing.

This is a very nice way to do asparagus, when you put it on the grill the little packets of foil puff right up. I really enjoyed this I love lemon and I love asparagus what a great combination. Thank you for posting. Made for the diabetic forum July 2011.

very good, I used a small package of baby carrots and used 2 tablespoons dry ranch dressing, I also added 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder, cooked in a convection oven for about 12 minutes, thanks for sharing Anme!

I made this Almond slivered bundt cake every Christmas especially for my Husband. it was a hit and he would be disappointed if I did not make this cake it was a favorite of his. I had not made the cake in fourteen years because of his passing and I lost the recipe, but remembered the cake. My daughter remembered having it at Christmas and now I am thrilled to have found this recipe again. It is truly delicious.
The crumbled bacon is definitely a good idea!  After one bite, my husband remarked that it tasted like a pizza and a baked potato had a baby:-). Very yummy comfort food!

Excellent dish! I made it for a party over Memorial weekend and everyone loved it! I left the cheese out, used Light Hellmans mayomaise, less bacon, and added raisens and some chopped walnuts. Next time I will try it with Turkey Bacon to make it lighter.

I made this last weekend and everyone really enjoyed it.  Even my mother who is known for her spaghetti sauce.  
I'm making it again today but didn't have crushed tomato sauce so I threw in some Barilla jarred sauce along with the fresh onion, garlic, black pepper and we'll see how it turns out.  Thanks for posting.

AMAZING! This is just like the BBQ beef at our favorite place next door. I made it exactly as written, and won't be making any changes. The kids thought it was a little spicy. Next time I will make them their own packet with less pepper. That's the great thing about this recipe, because of the foil I can make two but cook them together in the crock pot.
This pie tastes great, but needs cornstarch or more flour so the pieces will hold their shape. Delicious, though

Very nice flavors and it literally took me all of 5 minutes to put everything in the crockpot.  Next time I may choose a different cut of meat - the pork shoulder was very fatty (not my taste when it comes to meat) - overall, yummy!

I made this cake into 24 cupcakes for a birthday party we were hosting. The cake was very rich, chocolatey and delicious. I found the frosting to be a bit sweet, but it was still very tasty.
I couldn't really taste the Dr Pepper clearly, but the cake had a definite punch of spice to it, which I can only assume came from the Dr Pepper.
These cure a chocolate fix, that's for sure! We'll be making these again. Thank you!

My kids were never really fans of zucchini until I tried your recipe tonight.  They loved it!  Based on other reviews, I used less water when making the batter, but found it to be too thick to stir.  I ended up using the full amount of water and the batter turned out perfectly.  I also added a little onion powder to the mixture.  The zucchini sticks came out nice and crispy and the coating was delicious.  This is a definite 5-star in our household!

Instead of the coleslaw mix, I used 1/2-3/4 lg. head of cabbage, diced baby carrots, 1 heaping T. Tone's Chicken Base, 3 potatoes and 2-14 oz. packages of Kielbasa. My slower cooker was filled to the top with meat and veggies. I still used only 4 c. of broth and it made more juice as it cooked. DELICIOUS! My husband kept on commenting on how good this was!! Thanks for posting!

I am not giving a star rating since I made too many changes.  But I love the flexibility with this pizza!!  I used fresh dough from the bakery section of my supermarket, omitted the bacon and added sliced tomato and crushed garlic to the top.  My husband gave me great compliments and I absolutely loved the spinach and pepper jack combo!!

This is defenitley one of my more favorite dishes here on Zaar.  I used chicken breast cut into strips and marinated it for about 4 hours.  I then dipped the chicken in the ritz cracker crumbs, and baked it (so it wouldnt be too fattening) at 375 for 25 minutes.  I also added the jalapenos on top of the chicken strips while baking!  It was a great dish that required little time!  Thanks for a definite return on my menu!

This review is for the roasted green beans.  I was planning to do the beans with the vinaigrette, onions, and feta, but they didn't make it that far.  They were almost gone before the time dinner came around because my kids were sneaking green beans while they were playing a board game.  I'm sure the dressing is wonderful and hopefully I'll be able to try it someday.  Following a comment in Sackville's review, I roasted them for just a bit longer to soften up the beans a bit.  They were perfect at about 7 minutes pre- and post- stir.  Thanks Bev.

My mother has made these for over 20 years!!! I finally got the recipe from her a few years back, and this is EXACTLY how she made them, and EXACTLY what we always called them. This is an EXTEMELY easy recipe as my 8 and 11 yr. old girls love to help me make them. I even made them instead of cupcakes to take to school for my daughter's bday party.  I suggest this recipe to EVERYONE!!! Soooo yummmmmmy!!!  ~Kelly

I bought a food processor just so I could make this recipe. It was delicious as a rice substitute under Sesame Ginger Shrimp. Even my husband commented that it was the perfect texture and tasted great. This is easier to make than rice! I used a fresh head of cauliflower. After processing, I put in a microwave safe bowl, covered loosely and microwaved for 5 minutes, then added butter and salt. Perfect!
Excellent! So rich in flavor. served mine with sauteed baby carrots which were a nice compliment to the chicken. Thanks for the post!

I used cheddar cheese soup in lieu of the cream of mushroom and added sliced jalapenos to the cheese layer...a refreshingly nice change....my daughter who won't try a burrito loved it and wants it again...Taco pie oh my(LOL).  Thanks for sharing.
Yum! I used a rib eye steak and made this as directed. Simple, rich, and good. Thanks bmcnichol for a great dinner. Made for PAC Spring 2010.
So easy!  My husband took the leftovers to work and the smell of it being reheated in the lunchroom prompted the secretary to email me for the recipe!
OMG!!! Had this tonight after marinating it for 24hrs. AND this was beyond Delish!!! By far this is now our fam fav. I paired it with garlic/parm asparagus & loaded mashed. Fabulous meal.
These were lovely muffins, nice and moist with just the right texture, not too light or too dense. I would certainly make these again. I also left out the walnuts.

Fantastic, easy marinara recipe.  Really.  I did add 1/2 teaspoon of thyme and about 1/8 teaspoon fennel seeds and cut the oil in half to lighten the recipe.  So good!  Using canned crushed tomatoes instead of whole allows you to skip that step.  I will add this to my classics.
My Chessie loves these.  What more is there to say!  She also shared them with her friends for Christmas!

This recipe is a keeper.  My daughter and fiance took my husband and I to iPic theater in Pasadena CA and they served chicken spring rolls as an appetizer.  I fell in love with the flavor, I had to find out how to make them and I did through your website.  These were delicious.  I made them as the main meal.  Each family member received 4.  They were comfortably full. I only gave 4 stars because I would like to make these ahead but I was nervous because the recipe said to make and eat.  But other than that, I am completely sold.

I made my own onion soup mix and cream of soup and then made the roast.  I used coke instead of pepsi, as it is a little sweeter and it turned out really tasty and the roast was fall apart tender.  The family and I really enjoyed it and It will be made again!

I made this for Thanksgiving Day.
Everyone love it. I had everything on hand. We will be making this over and over. Thank You..Hugs

tasted like jack daniel's... which shouldnt be surprising i suppose, but that's ALL it tasted like. my boyfriend asked me, "did you dump a bunch of alcohol in this marinade? because that's what it tastes like!" uh oh

OMG we loved these. Granted, we marinated them for 2 days! LOL honestly, any more than 2 days and it probably would have been too potent. We even made chicken with the marinade the next night! Very very good. Kudos Kittencal!

This was delicious. At the 90min mark I added the tomato paste and spices and then poured the sauce over the uncooked meatballs in a 9x13 casserole dish. Popped them in the oven covered for 30min @ 375 then took the tinfoil off, added shredded cheese and baked for another 15 min. I also added about 1/2 cup of cream the the meatballs because I used ground venison, which is super lean.

I enjoyed this recipe 3 ways for Christmas with the fam. One exactly to the recipe, one with splenda, maple extract, and bacon, and the last as a triple layer in a spring form with a cheesecake layer and a streussel layer. All were wonderful, but none were the gorgeous bright orange of the photo. I prefer these to any pumpkin pie I've ever had.

Aunt Linda, I was looking for a new spaghetti sauce and came across yours.  I couldn't wait to make it as you made it one time when I was at your house and it was even better than my moms.  Shhh - Don't tell her that!. Cassie absolutely loved it and was raving about it to her mother when we went over there to bring her some of the leftovers.  She later called us and said it was better than hers!  Such good flavor and a great blend of ingredients for the perfect sauce.  Take it from an Italian, this one is "The One"!  So glad you posted it on here so I have it handy.  Mike

Made these last night with my Christmas Eve dinner.  They came out perfect and there was not a bean left.   Very easy to make and made the house smell good while cooking.   Thank you so much for posting.

Really rich and besides the orange color, you wouldn't know it's pumpkin. I told my husband it was Longhorn pasta and he ate it right up; he still has no idea. I used sage as I'm not a huge nutmeg fan and thinned with about a cup of chicken broth. Next time I'll probably replace all or part of the cream with evaporated skimmed milk to reduce the fat. Thanks, Mercy, for a recipe I'll use often!

This recipe was soooo easy and soooo fun.  We went wild, making several different colors.  The smell was great.  I found that the dough was sticky until it cooled a little.  I just mixed the water in the best I could, let it cool a little and then mixed more until I could knead it.  I didn't want to give the finished project over to the kids to play with because I wanted to keep playing with it.
Yummy! My family loved it and I even share with my friends. Made bite sizes so it turn into 2 dozen or more I think. I Added some choco chips.

This is my fifth time making this mac and cheese recipe, this Memorial Day! I come from a family of mac and cheese lovers, so I had to be sure it was a recipe my family would like. It was hard for me to change from my recipe I had for years, and years. The only issue I experienced is you must use a bigger pan than what they list 15 x 10. I also use Nature's Seasoning to give it a great flavor, instead of the white pepper. I also add a dollup more of sour cream and sprinkle some of what says Three Cheese (In the bag) before baking.
I didn't make yet. Should there be an adjustment for high altitude? Someone here recommended that after one hour lower it to 325°. Cover Loosely with foil for 15 minutes to prevent burning.

What a simple, tasty recipe. I made it as directed and grabbed the last can of cream of shrimp soup off of the grocery shelf, lol. I used fresh cauliflower because I had some on hand and served it over rice. Thanks for a nice dinner loof. Congrats again on your Divisional Football win!

Ah, the very last days of Summer, so my daughter and I decided to make this as a treat. It is a very good popsicle that does taste like a milkshake!  I was afraid as I was making this that the chocolate syrup that you pour into the mold before you pour the milk mixture, would stick to the mold and not the popsicle.  This was indeed what happened.  Next time I will just put the sprinkles in, or just a VERY small amount of syrup to make the sprinkles stick.  As it was, a few of the sprinkles were distributed throughout the popsicle, and that gave a nice effect.  Will definitely make these again!

This was really good - I did substitute 1 cup of prepared Tomato (pasta sauce - with garlic and fresh tomatoes) in place of the tomatos and spices - used half beef and half cheese tortellini, and only 1 cup of grated cheese. I did add fresh spinach instead of brocolli - just added it to the heated sauce.   The whole family loved it.  Easy to make additions or subtractions from.  Thanks!
This was a wonderful salsa that we enjoyed with pork and flour tortillas.  Full of flavour and really perked up the meal.  Thanks.

I used this recipe to use up some old crackers that had gone stale. I ground them up for 1 cup of the flour. This is part of a "kitchen cleanse" I am blogging on: http://kitchencleanse.blogspot.com/. I did not have any green onion on hand, so I used 2 garlic cloves very well minced instead and some onion powder. Maybe some chopped spinach instead of the onion next time

DELICIOUS! THIS IS A KEEPER!
I loved this dish and will be making this over & over again!  It is the bomb!

Loved it!  It's a pretty and colorful salad, and it was super easy to make.  It actually tasted even better after chilling for a few hours.  I made this exactly as written and used all the garnishes listed.  I think this is one of my new favorite bean salads.  Thanx!

I'll echo my love for the vibrancy of this salad!  I couldn't wait to eat it after mixing it together, but I must admit it was not as excellent as I thought it would be.  So, I left it to marinate and after a few hours in the fridge the taste was much improved.  Patience is critical!

I made these cookies twice and everyone loved them. I've tried making chocolate chip cookies before but they never turned out good. This recipe was recommended by a co-worker and they taste just as good as they look. I followed the recipe except for the amount of chocolate chips; personally taste really. I reduced it to a little over 2 cups and they turned out perfect. This is my number one chocolate chip recipe and I am grateful to have been introduced to it.
This was my son's birthday cake and everyone loved it.  I loved it too because it was simple and a cool treat on a hot day.  Thank you!

This Chicken recipe tasted great, my family really liked it. Also the left over chicked breast made great sandwiches on a kiaser rool.
It did take longer to prepare than the recipies I usually make but it was worth the effort!
This was incredibly easy to make and used items most of us have in the house (even us begginers :D ). My boyfriend was also happy with it too. This is something I will defintely be making again.
Delicious and easy. I didn't have all the exact ingredients, but substituted and it was great!
i made this tonight,and my family loved it.  my 15 year old picky eater loved it.  my family told me it's a keeper.

Excellent comforting!! I made 1/4 of the recipe for just myself. I used 1 teaspoon sugar, just a pinch not even a 1/4 teaspoon of saffron, 1 cardamom clove 3/4 cup water. Simmered for 20-30 minutes. I served in an espresso cup making for 2 refills. Thanks for the soothing drink. Made for http://www.food.com/bb/viewtopic.zsp?p=5341048#5341048 January's Tag Game ~ Saffron ~

These were too cute!   I used vienna fingers, because they were a dollar cheaper than the nutter butter cookies and about the same shape.  I had a difficult time dipping the cookies, so I ended up just using a knife and frosting them.  I am going to take them to the babysitters with my son on Halloween!

I think this is brilliant! The prep method is super, it tastes great and it's healthy! Whats not to like. Clearly it will help if you like garbanzo's (I love them). The texture is very pleasent and the pepper flakes give it a kick. It doesn't take long to make and served with  salad (I dressed mine very simply with lemon juice and a bit of salt) this makes a marvelous meal. Made for PAC, Fall'o7

I enjoyed this lovely dish for lunch today.  Served the delicious dip with nana bread.  Yumm so much flavor, quick and very easy to make, with terrific results.  Loved the flavors in the feta, the salt, lemon, basil and olive oil, so very tasty.  Made in Memory of Pammyowl.
These are great! I have made them a few times now.  Once with ground turkey.  I have also added black olives and corn.  They are super easy and very yummy!
Made these cookies and they remind me of eating pumpkin bread with oatmeal in it.  They are soft.  Like the taste.
I used this recipe today for adults and children and the resounding comments were that it wasn't sweet enough. Next time I will double the sugar and the cocoa powder and then review again.

What a super breakfast this made on Easter morning.  Loved the addition of the cream cheese, and I did make your apple syrup.  Had maple bacon and sausages and some fresh fruit!  Great recipe Annie, TY!

OH MY GOODNESS!!! What a wonderful treat this recipe is! I was a little leery about the dressing but it is SUPER. Served to a large group and had rave reviews from everyone.

Thank you for this article and all of the replies. Without them, not sure I would have tried this.

I made this for dinner one night and the kids thought I ordered take out....lol.  I love it when I get confused to resteraunt chefs....woohoo.  I thought this was so easy to prepare adn had a great taste.  I plan on making again when the pork tenderloins go on sale.  Thank you for  posting.

One of our new favorite weeknight meals when I need something fast or easy.  I've made it three times in the past two months and DH said he could have it once a week. Keeper, keeper, keeper!  Thanks!

My family loved these.  I spread them with the butter right off the griddle and thats all we topped them with.  I asked my family if they wanted some topping and they all said they are good like this.  That makes me LOVE this recipe. I never tasted it but it sure doesn''t look easy.  Toast is easy.

My husband loved them!  The only thing I changed was to not add the nuts.  I think this batter would hold up to many other additions.  I will be trying them with blueberries and other fruits.  My son picked these to take to school to for his birthday treat.  Hopefully the 3rd graders will love them too.  Thanks for posting!
This recipe is awesome!  My husband is a diabetic and has to watch his carbs.  He says this is even better than "real" pasta! He asks for it all the time.  We love it!

GREAT TASTING LITTLE PATTIES! I especially liked the combo of zucchini & corn, & will be making these again, especially when my vegetarian son & DIL come by! Thanks for sharing the recipe! [Tagged, made & reviewed as a PRESSIE in the Aus/NZ 12 Days of Christmas Recipe Swap]

Great pasta salad! I did cut the recipe in half for my family and they loved it. Used matchstick carrots, cut back on the olives and made the dressing the night before. So easy to make and the flavors together are wonderful. Made and reviewed for PAC 2007...thank you Messy44.
I'm not much of a fish fan but this quick and easy recipe made for a wonderfully relaxing meal. Have to be careful when cooking the fish in the microwave as mine almost overcooked it/dried it out.

Seriously, I amazed, I always cross my fingers praying for the best when I make a new cookie. I'm a pretty good cook. But when it comes to baking it's kinda hit or miss for me. And ta da!! These cookies are a complete SUCCESS. Thank you for the recipe can't wait to make more. Kid tested, mother approved. Happy Holidays all!

Good recipe with great flavor.  I used 1/2 halibut and 1/2 small scallops. I only used 1/2 green pepper, 1 jalapeno and 1/2 onion and that was more than enough of each.  Used avocado for garnish, not sure if I would like the olives.
This recipe has become a family favorite!!!!!  Whenever company is over and I happen to be making this, they ALWAYS want the recipe! Absolutely love it.  The peanutty sauce is fantastic.

This was wonderful, Very easy to put together. I followed the recipe to a T and, Everyone at the dinner party enjoyed it.
I will make this again and still no changes. there is no need its perfect.
Thanks so much for suggesting this and Jen T's recipe as well.
Its a keeper.

I became a member just to say how great this is!  I did nothing different except I put it in the fridge bacause the freezer was too full.  We thought it got better day by day so I'll make it a day ahead next time.  Great Great Great!
I doubled the recipe to bring to a family gathering. It easily doubles in the 9 X 13 pan. It was delicious! This is the best peach crisp recipe I've tried yet.
My husband enjoyed these with his steak tonight. I used all beef broth as I didn't have any wine. These were quick and easy to make. Next time I would add onions to the mix.

This is wonderful! The butter is to die for! I have been craving steaks and this just fit the bill perfectly. I marinated the steaks for most of the day before dinner. Just delicious. Made for ZWT4 for the Tastebud Tickling Travellers.

You've been adopted during Pick-A-Chef Fall 2012!

These turned out brilliantly, soft and mushy on theinside and lovely and crispy on the outside.... my husband has asked me to make my potatoes like this more often... definately a keeper... thanks jewelies

Stacky, the recipe sounds great and the franks in the photo look delicious.  Can you tell me the brand name?  Thanks!

I made this for my son's birthday.  It was so easy and very moist.  Good recipe.
This was the easiest and tastiest chicken recipie I can recall.  It's great as leftovers as well.  You can have it cold with salad or tortilla or hot over rice.  My husband and I loved it.

I made a simple Brown Irish Soda Bread#179821 to go with it.  This is definitely going in my regular rotation of meals.  Thank you!
This was really good.  I followed the recipe exactly and was very pleased with the outcome.  I think the cheese toast really made the dish.  I will be making this again.

My wife and I love it. She has made it with herbed cream cheese as well and while it is good, I prefer the Boursin. We have made it for company and gotten nothing but raves. Great way to keep carbs down and up fiber.
We thoroughly enjoyed this salad! The dressing is amazing!  Very easy to make also! Will make often! Thanks!!!!!!!! (Also did not refridgerate the dressing; it was fine!)

This sounded really good so I decided to make it. I did find the prep to be longer than 15 min. but the end result was worth it (I did 3 separate batches of chicken so it took awhile). I made this and took it to work the other day.  One of my male co-workers tasted it and said "Boy, it's a good thing you're married."  This was so yummy! I have made these many times, and even my non-dieting husband enjoys these for dinner.
This recipe worked great for me. I thought it would be crumbly, too, when the dough separated into layers when I put them onto the cookie sheet, but they turned out just fine. Soft and delicious!

Addictive! I made this Saturday night and it was gone pretty quick. I did not put peanuts or cherrios in and it was still great! In fact I made 2 batches, the first one I didn't bake in oven... the sauce was sooo good. The 2nd batch I baked and it was yummy! Great recipe!
My family really loved this recipe.  I used a wine called Colombo marsala (dry).

YUM.  I didn't use my food processor, but this whipped up pretty fast anyway.  Nice and biscotti-like on the outside, but a little cookierier on the inside. 
A new favorite for our family.

Thanks CountryLady. It was very tasty, though quite messy to make. Everybody here enjoyed it very much. I added quite a lot of tomato sauce to make it more thick.

I can't believe all the reviews people are writing. I mean, how in the world did you people taste them? I've made two batches, but you can't pick them up with a fork or a spoon. This was refreshing and made a nice treat. I did blend it for awhile to get it nice and thick. Thanks for sharing. Made for Every Day is a Holiday tag.

If you like jello, then this is to die for!  I just begged this recipe from a friend who had brought it to a potluck.  Yum, yum, yum!!

I bet this will be great light;y toasted on a winter morning.

Uuummmm and so easy! I thick sliced my potatoes (1/2") on the bottom of a greased crock pot, on the stove I browned the chops well in bacon grease...yeah I know...layered them over the potatoes. This is my favorite marinade!  I've used it for lamb chops twice and for steaks two times now. This recipe is easy and amazing. I actually made them for a friend's house party and everyone loved it. Thanks!

Totally amazing! Even though mine looked nothing like the little nuggets in the picture who cares. It tastes so good I took it to work and we ate almost the whole batch in one day! It was so easy I probably will never buy granola again. Thanks for a winner!!

YUM!  I used flounder in this recipe and I made a couple of substitutions...I used cereal crumbs instead of the bread crumbs and since my family isn't too keen on onions, and I only had Italian dressing mix in the house, that's what I used. I took this to a brunch and people were fighting over second helpings!  It's healthy, delicious and quick & easy to make.  Even better when the flavours blend on day two!  Thanks!
I made this for my nephew and I for lunch today and we really enjoyed it. We did not have sage sausage, so I added sage seasoning to the dish. Thanks for a great recipe. :)

Delish! I tried these in the oven (350F for 1 hour) and they made my kitchen smell great! They were simple and very tasty. Thanks diner for sharing.

First of all this is a easy recipe to make. It smells good in and out of the oven. It is a very pretty on the table and taste great. Next time I will add Salt and pepper. My wife and I thank the chef for the recipe.
Great recipe. My first sorbet, I'm eating some now. It's soo smooth. I added the juice of 1 lemon and a little lemon zest.

My sister-in-law brought this to a family dinner and I loved it!  She told me what was in it so I had to track down the recipe.  It's a keeper and so easy to boot.

I also finely minced one clove of garlic and added it about a minute before the onions were brown. It was delicious!!! Thanks for reminding me how it's done!

my family doesn't like eggnog...changed it to half and half, added a splash of vanilla extract and decorated with red and green sugar sprinkles/cinnamon mix....they were gone before I could get one!!!

We really enjoyed these carrots. I had to use frozen sliced carrots and juice from 2 tangerines but it worked perfectly. Next time, I'll use the baby carrots because the photo looks so nice. Thanks Barb for sharing this great recipe.

I make with salt instead of Old Bay, and also the addition of 2 tbsp. chopped fresh parsley (or 1 tsp. dried) added with the thyme.   Yummy!   Fits well in an 8 by 8 baking dish.   Let it stand for about 30 minutes before serving it.

Terrific flavor. To cut at least some of the fat I used 3/4 cup of cream and 2 cups of whole milk so mine was less "ultimate" but still very good. The recipe worked well using all Splenda. After reading Boomies recipe I cooked the pecans first (no way were they going to absorb all of the butter and I used 3 Tbsp instead of 4) and set them in the freezer while I mixed up the vanilla base. Once they were cool I put them into the fridge to chill along with the mix for 20 mins. The ice cream took about 20 mins to soft freeze in the machine and I just stirred the prepared pecans into the ice cream once it was in the container for ripening.

These are really good.  The first batch I cooked off were ok...and then I noticed I hadn't added the cheese.  I did add quite a bit of salt,  but I will make again.  They also didn't raise my sugars,  which is a huge plus.  Oh,  and I added more onion,  green onion,  fresh parsley,  and some swiss chard just to use up more produce from the garden...just chopped it all up well.
Delicious recipe! tried it with the family and the orzo wasn't the biggest hit, but the meatballs were gobbled up in a heartbeat. would definitely recommend.

Very Very Good - Very Simple Quick - Easy - and Tasty! I Will be making this many - many more times. I only made tiny changes, I put cumin in my Mac 'N Cheese and I only had regular bacon that I cooked and chopped up in small bits. I also added a tad of cilantro. It was all very nice! I plan on trying it with other kinds of meat, like tuna, shredded turkey and maybe even corn beef. Thank You So Very Much!!
I agree with Jenny, the potatoes should be cooked first before attempting this recipe. Just got the amchur powder from an online site, (ishopindian.com), and it is excellent for dishes like this one.

I just have to give 5 start to this recipe. It adapted very well to my diabetic changes: used whole wheat flour and Porridge Oats which are a mix of large oat flakes, oat bran, wheat bran and flax seed. I also used no sugar added maple flavored syrup. They rose beautifully and are very tender and moist inside. I love that they aren't over sweet but if you have a sweet tooth you'll want to increase the syrup (allow for moisture changes) or add some sugar. The natural PB is the only kind I ever use and the flavor came through in just the right amount.

What a great recipe! The texture is almost cake-like, as if pastry flour had been used instead of all-purpose; and it couldn't be more moist. A classic; so easy to make. I won't be looking at other banana bread recipes. This one goes into my file.

How easy and delicious is this!!!!!   What a great topping.  I used this on top of spice cake but this topping can be used on just about anything.  Thanks so much for sharing, MarraMamba.  Also, thank YOU for trying one my my recipes (Easy Taco Stew).  I am so glad you enjoyed it.

Loved this recipe!  I cut the chicken into bite sized pieces and served it over brown rice.

The only change I made were to double the sauce, and use the juice of the orange I zested instead of the concentrate.

I really enjoyed this recipe! I did add alittle Mrs.Dash Garlic and Herb seasoning and alittle black pepper to the cornmeal and added bits of butter over top of fillets. I didn't have butter flavored cooking spray so I used Pam with Olive Oil. I baked this at 350'  for 20 minutes. 
Thanks for sharing the recipe! :)

We live in Johannesburg, South Africa, and though available, salsa is fairly expensive.  My daughter LOVES salsa, so I have been trying recipes from Zaar.  This has been our favourite so far.  My husband says "Old El Paso, move over.  :)  It is full of flavour, and has a wonderful, runny consistency, which we prefer over the really chunky.  Thanks for a great recipe.

This is a great pie! Coconut Creme Pie is my father in law's absolute hands down favorite dessert. This one blew him away. I had never made one before so for him I thought I would give it a try. Very easy and tasted great, I doubled the recipe so he could take one home as well.

We completely enjoyed this smooth, creamy sauce over linguine.  DD and DH both thought it could use a little herbal touch, possibly some finely chopped parsely, cilantro, or basil; we garnished it with cilantro which blended marvelously with the garlic.  We will be making this again.
This is a great, simple recipe.  I liked the combo of melty-american & tangy swiss.  I also like a big dash of worsterchire (?) on top & a slather of mustard.  THANKS!
Very good and flavorful -- really enjoyed it.  Thanks!

Don't be afraid to add less than 1/2 cup white sugar, & a little more Mccormick vanilla flavor. Delicious!! These peanut butter cookies are amazingly delicious. My family loves them made 3 separate batches already in 1 day. I've sent the receipe to family members to please try. Well, what are you waiting for, you got cookies to bake. Enjoy!

Sweet with a hint of ginger.  Just perfect.  These are great for kids and "grown-up" enough for adults.  I may have used a bit extra ginger; I didn't measure it.  Thanx for sharing this.  I'll be making these again.
Super easy and rave reviews from everyone, it also made a ton so there were a lot to share.  I would definitely make again!
